Now, again, I'm not a demographer, but - and I hope the Trial Chamber will hear testimony on this issue - I don't think it's possible to make sense, if I may use that term, out of drawing borders which would encompass 65 per cent of the territory of the Republic but still be predominantly Serbian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I actually had in mind, Mr. Treanor, just tell me if this is just totally wrong. After all, you're giving evidence, and that's your prerogative, to express your view. But what I had in mind was this: That if Bosnia is transformed and there is then a separate Serb Republic as part of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, for the Serb Republic to end up as an entity in which the Serbs were in a minority would surely have simply laid the foundations for the same problems to emerge again another year in the future.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, indeed. And as I thought I indicated, in their terms, that would not have made sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Excuse me one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm coming on now to really rather a large discrete topic to the question of the -- I was planning to go next to the question of the six strategic objectives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Six minutes, that might not be enough for six strategic objectives.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The question is -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have a smaller subject you could deal with in five minutes, we'd like to hear that. If not, then we'll adjourn for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, I don't, Your Honour. That is really the next point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Before we adjourn, it would be helpful, if possible, for some forecasting of our schedule for the remainder of the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I believe that we are fairly well on track. We've got tomorrow afternoon and Friday morning, and I had indicated to the Tribunal and earlier to the Prosecution that I expected to be, as far as I could estimate, all or most of this week with Mr. Treanor. I feel as confident as one can reasonably be that I am going to finish with Mr. Treanor this week. I also don't feel it's at all likely that I will finish with him tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We might have to find time as well for a few procedural issues, but I'd rather leave them until the cross-examination of Mr. Treanor has been finished. First of all, there's your letter, which might need some attention, then another issue might be adjudicated facts on which the Chamber would like to -- perhaps would like to briefly discuss the way of dealing with that and procedurally with the parties. So it's uncertain whether we would find time before the weekend to deal with these issues, but your estimate is that somewhere on Friday you'd be able to conclude your cross-examination, then of course it also depends on how many questions there are from the Bench and whether this would trigger any new questions from the parties. But, Mr. Tieger, is this sufficient guidance?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think that's -- I understand that -- sorry. I understand that that's the best estimate that counsel can offer, and I appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Then we adjourn for the day. We will sit tomorrow, Thursday, at a quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of April, 2004, at 2.15 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
